outcome: Composite maternal outcome (postpartum hemorrhage or third- or fourth-degree perineal tears)
Composite neonatal outcome (shoulder dystocia or brachial plexus injury)
cohort: Singleton pregnancies who underwent vaginal delivery in a university-affiliated tertiary hospital (1996-2015), excluding pregnancies complicated by diabetes mellitus, fetal anomalies or cesarean deliveries (n=26,920)
finding: For non-diabetic mothers who deliver vaginally, neonatal birth weight ≥ 4400 g was associated with a significant increase in adverse neonatal outcomes, whereas neonatal birth weight ≥ 4800 g was associated with a significant increase in adverse maternal outcomes.
